content:
Back and spinal arthritis (including spondylosis and facet joint OA) affects a large proportion of UK adults over 50. NICE recommends exercise as a core treatment, and a structured 12-week programme can reduce back pain by 25–40% — comparable to standard analgesia.

Quick answer: Exercise is a core treatment for back arthritis, offering significant pain reduction comparable to medication. Recommended exercises include deep-core strengthening (pelvic tilts, bird-dog, glute bridges), spinal mobility (cat-cow, knee-to-chest), and low-impact aerobic activities like walking, cycling, or swimming. These help nourish discs, strengthen stabilising muscles, and improve posture without accelerating spinal degeneration.

Why Exercise Is Essential for Back Arthritis

Regular movement nourishes intervertebral discs, strengthens the deep core and back extensors that stabilise the spine, improves posture, and slows progression. The most common concern — "will exercise damage my spine?" — has a clear evidence-based answer: appropriate, graded exercise does not accelerate spinal degeneration and is the most effective non-surgical treatment.

Strengthening Exercises

1. Pelvic Tilts

Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Gently flatten the lower back into the floor by tilting the pelvis. Hold 5 seconds. Repeat 10 times. 2–3 sets.

2. Bird-Dog

On hands and knees, extend opposite arm and leg slowly. Hold 5 seconds. Lower with control. 8–10 reps each side. 2 sets.

3. Glute Bridges

Lying on your back with knees bent, lift the hips towards the ceiling, squeezing the glutes. Hold 5 seconds. 10–12 reps. 2–3 sets.

4. Wall Squats (Partial)

Back against a wall, slide down to a quarter-squat. Hold 10 seconds. Build to 30 seconds. 3 sets.

Mobility Exercises

5. Cat-Cow

On hands and knees, alternate between arching and rounding the back smoothly. 10 slow cycles. Do daily.

6. Knee-to-Chest Stretch

Lying on your back, gently draw one knee to the chest. Hold 20 seconds. Swap sides. 3 each side.

7. Lower-Back Rotation

Knees bent, drop both knees gently to one side, then the other. 10 cycles. Keep shoulders down.

Aerobic Exercises

Walking, stationary cycling and swimming (especially backstroke) are the most studied low-impact options for back arthritis. Aim for 30 minutes most days, which can be split into 3 × 10-minute sessions.

Back Exercises for Osteoarthritis

For spinal OA and spondylosis, the priority is deep-core strengthening (transverse abdominis activation, bird-dog) combined with hip-flexor mobility and low-impact aerobic work. NICE places this alongside weight management as the core treatment. See our osteoarthritis exercises guide and osteoarthritis treatment overview.

Back Exercises for Rheumatoid Arthritis

RA can affect the cervical spine in particular. During flares, restrict to gentle mobility only and avoid loaded extension. Hydrotherapy in warm water (33–35 °C) is well tolerated. Full programme: rheumatoid arthritis exercises.

Gentle Back Exercises for Severe Arthritis

Pelvic tilts, supported knee-to-chest, cat-cow and pool walking allow you to keep the spine moving without overloading it. Two short 10-minute daily sessions are better tolerated than one longer one.

Exercises to Avoid With Back Arthritis

Avoid heavy deadlifts, loaded spinal flexion (sit-ups, weighted toe-touches), high-impact running with severe OA and unsupported overhead pressing. Swap for partial squats, bird-dog, glute bridges and stationary cycling. For a personalised plan, find a back physiotherapist near you.

Back Arthritis Exercise FAQ — People Also Ask

What are the best exercises for an arthritic back?

The best routine combines deep-core strengthening (pelvic tilts, bird-dog, glute bridges), spinal mobility (cat-cow, knee-to-chest) and low-impact aerobic work (walking, cycling, swimming). Done 3–4 times per week, this can reduce back pain by 25–40%.

How often should I do back exercises for arthritis?

Strengthening 2–3 times per week, mobility daily (5–10 minutes), aerobic 3–5 times per week (30 minutes, can be split into 3 × 10 min).

Can exercise cure back arthritis?

No, but it is the most effective non-surgical treatment for spinal OA and can delay or avoid the need for spinal injections or surgery. Benefits stop if exercise stops.

What exercises should I avoid with back arthritis?

Avoid heavy deadlifts, loaded sit-ups, high-impact running with severe OA and unsupported overhead pressing. Stick to partial squats, bird-dog and stationary cycling.

Are there gentle back exercises for severe arthritis?

Yes — pelvic tilts, supported knee-to-chest, cat-cow, pool walking and stationary cycling on low resistance. Two short 10-minute daily sessions are usually better tolerated.

How long until back exercises reduce arthritis pain?

Reduced stiffness within 2–3 weeks, meaningful pain reduction at 6–8 weeks, full benefit at 12 weeks of consistent practice.

Practical next steps for Best Exercises for Back Arthritis: A Complete UK Physiotherapy Guide

If you came here about Best Exercises for Back Arthritis: A Complete UK Physiotherapy Guide, pick one change you can keep for a fortnight rather than overhauling everything at once. Note what hurts, what helps, and what you have already tried, then take that list to your GP, rheumatology nurse or physiotherapist so the conversation stays concrete.

In many areas you can ask your primary care network about self-referral to physiotherapy or lifestyle support without waiting for a hospital letter. Check your GP surgery website or the NHS App for the route that applies where you live.

Pacing on good and bad days

On better days it is tempting to catch up on everything at once. Spread chores and exercise across the week instead. Use the two-hour rule many physiotherapists suggest: if pain or fatigue is clearly worse two hours after activity, the dose was too high — trim the next session rather than stopping altogether.

Building a joint-friendly routine

Start with short sessions you can repeat on most days. Warm water, cycling, or paced walking often suits stiff joints better than sudden high-impact bursts. Increase time or resistance slowly, and leave a rest day when a joint is hot, swollen or unusually painful. If you are unsure where to begin, ask about NHS physiotherapy or an exercise referral scheme via your GP surgery.

Preparing for appointments

Write three priorities before you go: main symptom, functional limit (stairs, sleep, work), and the question you most need answered. Bring a current medicine list including over-the-counter products. If English is not your first language, request an interpreter when you book.

Working with NHS pathways

Most people start with GP care, community physiotherapy and self-management, with rheumatology involved when inflammatory disease is suspected or treatment needs escalate. Ask what monitoring blood tests or reviews you should expect, and who to contact between appointments if a flare escalates.

Peer support etiquette

Share what helps you without prescribing it for others. Conditions, medicines and life circumstances differ. If someone is in crisis, encourage them toward NHS 111, their GP, or emergency services rather than relying on a forum alone.

Quick questions about Best Exercises Back Arthritis

Is this a substitute for seeing a clinician? No. Use it to prepare questions and understand options, then confirm decisions with your NHS team.

How long before I judge whether a change helped? Give most habit or exercise changes at least two to four weeks, unless pain or swelling clearly worsens — in that case scale back sooner.

What should I track? Joint pain (0–10), morning stiffness time, sleep quality, and how far you can walk or how long you can type or stand. Patterns beat one-off ratings.

Safety and when to get urgent help

This page is general information for people in the United Kingdom, not personal medical advice. Seek urgent help via NHS 111 or A&E if you have sudden inability to move a joint, hot swollen joint with fever, chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or symptoms that feel immediately dangerous.
